section_1.title: The Cheetah’s Paradox: Average vs. Instant
section_1.content: Introduce the difference between 'average speed' over a journey and 'speed at a single moment.' Hook the audience by asking how a speedometer knows your speed if you haven't traveled a distance yet.
section_1.example: A cheetah sprints 100 meters in 4 seconds. Its average speed is 25m/s. However, at exactly 2.5 seconds, was it accelerating or slowing down? We need a way to find the speed at that exact 'frozen' frame.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: The Slope of a Secant Line
section_2.content: Review the concept of slope (rise over run) between two points on a curve. This represents the average rate of change. Visually represent this as a 'Secant Line' cutting through a graph.
section_2.example: On a distance-time graph (y = x²), draw a line connecting Point A (1, 1) and Point B (3, 9). Slope = (9-1)/(3-1) = 4. This is the average speed between 1 and 3 seconds.

section_3.title: The 'Zooming In' Technique (The Limit Concept)
section_3.content: Animate Point B moving closer and closer to Point A. As the interval (h) between the points shrinks toward zero, the secant line rotates and begins to look like it only touches the curve at one point.
section_3.example: Visualizing the interval shrinking: first from 2 seconds, then 1 second, then 0.1, 0.01... until the two points are nearly overlapping. The gap 'h' is vanishing.

section_4.title: The Birth of the Derivative
section_4.content: Define the Instantaneous Rate of Change as the slope of the 'Tangent Line.' Introduce the formal limit definition of the derivative: f'(x) = lim (h->0) [f(x+h) - f(x)] / h.
section_4.example: A magnifying glass zooms into the curve until the curved line looks like a perfectly straight flat line. The slope of this straight 'micro-segment' is the derivative at that point.

section_5.title: The 'Power' in Action
section_5.content: Demonstrate the power of the derivative as a function that gives the slope at any point. Show that we no longer need to calculate 'rise over run' manually if we know the derivative rule.
section_5.example: If the cheetah's position is f(t) = t², its speed at any time 't' is f'(t) = 2t. At exactly 3 seconds, the cheetah is going exactly 6 m/s. We have turned a static curve into a dynamic measurement of change.

section_6.title: Summary: The Snapshot of Change
section_6.content: Recap that the derivative is the 'instantaneous' version of a rate of change. It is the bridge between algebra (two points) and calculus (one point).
section_6.example: Visual recap: A car driving on a hilly road. The steepness of the hill at the exact spot the tires touch the ground is the derivative of the road's height.

section_4.example: A magnifying glass zooms into the curve until the curved line looks like a perfectly straight flat line. The slope of this straight 'micro-segment' is the derivative at that point.

section_5.title: The 'Power' in Action
section_5.content: Demonstrate the power of the derivative as a function that gives the slope at any point. Show that we no longer need to calculate 'rise over run' manually if we know the derivative rule.
section_5.example: If the cheetah's position is f(t) = t², its speed at any time 't' is f'(t) = 2t. At exactly 3 seconds, the cheetah is going exactly 6 m/s. We have turned a static curve into a dynamic measurement of change.

section_6.title: Summary: The Snapshot of Change
section_6.content: Recap that the derivative is the 'instantaneous' version of a rate of change. It is the bridge between algebra (two points) and calculus (one point).
section_6.example: Visual recap: A car driving on a hilly road. The steepness of the hill at the exact spot the tires touch the ground is the derivative of the road's height.

section_1.title: The Cheetah’s Paradox: Average vs. Instant
lecture_lines: A cheetah sprints across the savanna.
Average speed is total distance over total time.
But how fast is it at one exact moment?
A speedometer shows speed at a single frozen instant.
This is the mystery of instantaneous rate of change.
animations: Animate a stylized cheetah icon moving across the screen from 0 to 100 on a scale.
Display a horizontal line labeled '100 meters' (#FFFFFF) and a timer finishing at '4.0s' (#FFFFFF).
Show the text 'Average Speed = 25 m/s' in #2ECC71 below the scale.
Abruptly freeze the cheetah's motion at the 2.5s mark.
Highlight the cheetah with a pulse effect in #FF0000 and label it 'Instant Speed?'.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: The Slope of a Secant Line
lecture_lines: On a graph, average speed is a secant line.
It connects two points to find the slope.
Slope equals the change in y over change in x.
animations: Draw a smooth curve representing f(x) = x^2 in #3498DB.
Plot and label Point A at (1,1) and Point B at (3,9) in #F1C40F.
Draw a straight 'Secant Line' in #E74C3C connecting points A and B.

section_3.title: The 'Zooming In' Technique (The Limit Concept)
lecture_lines: Let's move the second point closer to the first.
The interval between them, h, starts to shrink.
As h approaches zero, the secant line rotates.
Zooming in, the curve begins to look straight.
The two points eventually merge into one.
animations: Show the curve from section 2 with Point A and Point B.
Label the horizontal gap between A and B as 'h' in #2ECC71.
Animate Point B sliding down the curve toward Point A.
Shrink the 'h' label and its associated horizontal line toward zero.
Rotate the Secant Line (#E74C3C) dynamically as Point B moves closer to A.

section_4.title: The Birth of the Derivative
lecture_lines: This single-point slope is the tangent line's slope.
We call this instantaneous rate the derivative.
Mathematically, it is the limit as h reaches zero.
The formula captures change at a specific moment.
This is the foundation of all calculus.
animations: Show Point B overlapping Point A, making the interval 'h' vanish.
Transform the Secant Line into a purple 'Tangent Line' (#9B59B6) touching only Point A.
Fade in the formal limit definition: f'(x) = lim(h->0) [f(x+h)-f(x)]/h in #FFFFFF.
Highlight the 'lim(h->0)' part of the formula in #F1C40F.
Pulse the Tangent Line to emphasize it represents the 'Instantaneous Rate'.

section_5.title: The 'Power' in Action
lecture_lines: Derivative rules let us find speed at any time.
For distance t squared, the speed is 2t.
Calculus turns static graphs into dynamic measurements.
animations: Display the function f(t) = t^2 in #3498DB at the top of the screen.
Animate a transition where f(t) = t^2 becomes f'(t) = 2t in #2ECC71.
Show the calculation 'At t = 3, Speed = 2(3) = 6 m/s' appearing in #FFFFFF.

section_6.title: Summary: The Snapshot of Change
lecture_lines: The derivative is a snapshot of change.
It bridges the gap between two points and one.
Now you know the secret behind the speedometer.
animations: Draw a winding hilly road curve in #95A5A6.
Draw three distinct Tangent Lines (#F1C40F) at different peaks and valleys of the road.
Display the concluding text 'Derivative: The Snapshot of Change' in #FFFFFF at the center.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary: The Snapshot of Change", [
            "- The derivative is a snapshot of change.",
            "- It bridges the gap between two points and one.",
            "- Now you know the secret behind the speedometer."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Draw a winding hilly road curve in #95A5A6.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Road function: y = f(x)
        # x range: grid center is ~3.0, range ~[0.5, 5.5]
        # y range: grid center is ~-0.3, range ~[-2.8, 2.2]
        def road_func(t):
            # t goes from -1 to 1
            x = 3.0 + 2.5 * t
            y = -0.3 + 1.2 * np.sin(3 * t) + 0.5 * np.cos(5 * t)
            return np.array([x, y, 0])

        road = ParametricFunction(road_func, t_range=[-1, 1], color="#95A5A6")
        self.play(Create(road), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Draw three distinct Tangent Lines (#F1C40F) at different points of the road.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Slope m = (dy/dt) / (dx/dt)
        # dy/dt = 1.2 * 3 * cos(3t) - 0.5 * 5 * sin(5t)
        # dx/dt = 2.5
        def get_tangent_line(t_val, length=1.2):
            point = road_func(t_val)
            slope_dy_dt = 3.6 * np.cos(3 * t_val) - 2.5 * np.sin(5 * t_val)
            slope_dx_dt = 2.5
            m = slope_dy_dt / slope_dx_dt
            
            # Direction vector
            direction = np.array([1, m, 0])
            direction = direction / np.linalg.norm(direction)
            
            start = point - direction * (length / 2)
            end = point + direction * (length / 2)
            return Line(start, end, color="#F1C40F", stroke_width=4)

        # Pick some points t for tangents
        tangents = VGroup(
            get_tangent_line(-0.8),
            get_tangent_line(0.0),
            get_tangent_line(0.7)
        )
        
        for tg in tangents:
            self.play(Create(tg), run_time=0.8)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Display the concluding text 'Derivative: The Snapshot of Change' in #FFFFFF at the center.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        concluding_text = Text("Derivative:\nThe Snapshot of Change", color="#FFFFFF", font_size=32)
        # Place in the center area of the right side grid
        self.place_in_area(concluding_text, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        # Add a subtle background to the text to ensure readability over the road
        bg_rect = BackgroundRectangle(concluding_text, color=BLACK, fill_opacity=0.7, buff=0.3)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(bg_rect), Write(concluding_text))
        self.wait(3)
        
        # Final Highlight
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(2)

            "- Slope equals the change in y over change in x."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Colors from storyboard
        COLOR_CURVE = "#3498DB"

        ).add_coordinates()
        self.place_in_area(axes, "A1", "F6")
        
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: x**2, x_range=[0, 3.2], color=COLOR_CURVE)
        curve_label = MathTex("f(x) = x^2", font_size=24, color=COLOR_CURVE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===

        point_a_coords = axes.c2p(1, 1)

        dot_a = Dot(point_a_coords, color=COLOR_POINTS)
        dot_b = Dot(point_b_coords, color=COLOR_POINTS)
        
        label_a = MathTex("A(1,1)", font_size=20, color=COLOR_POINTS).next_to(dot_a, DL, buff=0.1)

            Write(label_a),

        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_SECANT)
        
        secant_line = Line(point_a_coords, point_b_coords, color=COLOR_SECANT)
        
        # Adding slope math for clarity as per outline example

        slope_math = MathTex(
            "m = \\frac{9-1}{3-1} = 4",
            font_size=24,
            color=COLOR_SECANT
        )
        self.place_at_grid(slope_math, "F4")

        self.play(Create(secant_line))
        self.play(Write(slope_math))
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Reset color
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(2)

import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)

        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):

        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):

        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard
        title_text = "The Birth of the Derivative"
        lecture_lines = [
            "This single-point slope is the tangent line's slope.",
            "We call this instantaneous rate the derivative.",
            "Mathematically, it is the limit as h reaches zero.",
            "The formula captures change at a specific moment.",
            "This is the foundation of all calculus."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Colors from storyboard and requirements
        TANGENT_COLOR = "#9B59B6"
        HIGHLIGHT_COLOR = "#F1C40F"
        FORMULA_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"

        # Setup Geometry (Right Side)
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-0.5, 4, 1],
            y_range=[-0.5, 4, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_tip": False}
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "C3", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        func = lambda x: 0.25 * (x**2)
        curve = axes.plot(func, x_range=[0, 4], color=BLUE)
        
        x_a = 1.2
        h_tracker = ValueTracker(1.5)
        
        dot_a = Dot(axes.c2p(x_a, func(x_a)), color=RED)
        label_a = MathTex("A", font_size=24).next_to(dot_a, DOWN + LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        # Dot B depends on h
        dot_b = Dot(color=WHITE)
        dot_b.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(axes.c2p(x_a + h_tracker.get_value(), func(x_a + h_tracker.get_value()))))
        
        label_b = MathTex("B", font_size=24)
        label_b.add_updater(lambda m: m.next_to(dot_b, RIGHT, buff=0.1))
        
        # Secant line extended
        secant_line = Line(color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        def update_secant(m):
            p1 = dot_a.get_center()
            p2 = dot_b.get_center()
            dist = np.linalg.norm(p2 - p1)
            if dist < 0.01:
                return
            v = (p2 - p1) / dist
            # Extend the line visually
            m.put_start_and_end_on(p1 - 1.0 * v, p1 + 3.0 * v)
        
        secant_line.add_updater(update_secant)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show Point B overlapping Point A, making the interval 'h' vanish.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.add(axes, curve, dot_a, label_a, dot_b, label_b, secant_line)
        self.play(h_tracker.animate.set_value(0.01), run_time=3)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Transform the Secant Line into a purple 'Tangent Line' (#9B59B6) touching only Point A.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Calculate slope for final tangent line
        slope_val = 0.5 * x_a # d/dx(0.25x^2) = 0.5x
        tangent_line = Line(
            axes.c2p(x_a - 1.0, func(x_a) - 1.0 * slope_val),
            axes.c2p(x_a + 3.0, func(x_a) + 3.0 * slope_val),
            color=TANGENT_COLOR,
            stroke_width=4
        )
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(dot_b),
            FadeOut(label_b),
            ReplacementTransform(secant_line, tangent_line),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Fade in the formal limit definition: f'(x) = lim(h->0) [f(x+h)-f(x)]/h in #FFFFFF.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Use split parts for highlighting later
        formula_parts = MathTex(
            "f'(x) =", "\\lim_{h \\to 0}", "\\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}",
            color=FORMULA_COLOR,
            font_size=32
        )
        self.place_in_area(formula_parts, "A2", "B5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(formula_parts))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Highlight the 'lim(h->0)' part of the formula in #F1C40F.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        self.play(formula_parts[1].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Pulse the Tangent Line to emphasize it represents the 'Instantaneous Rate'.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        self.play(
            tangent_line.animate.scale(1.1).set_stroke(width=6),
            rate_func=there_and_back,
            run_time=1.5
        )

            "- Slope equals the change in y over change in x."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        COLOR_POINTS = "#F1C40F"

        label_a = MathTex("A(1,1)", font_size=20, color=COLOR_POINTS).next_to(dot_a, DL, buff=0.1)
        label_b = MathTex("B(3,9)", font_size=20, color=COLOR_POINTS).next_to(dot_b, UL, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(dot_a, dot_b),
            Write(label_a),
            Write(label_b)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===

        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)

        # Adding slope math for clarity as per outline example

        slope_math = MathTex(
            "m = \\frac{9-1}{3-1} = 4",
            font_size=24,
            color=COLOR_SECANT
        )
        self.place_at_grid(slope_math, "F4")

        self.play(Create(secant_line))
        self.play(Write(slope_math))
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Reset color
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(2)

outline.title: The Cheetah’s Paradox: Average vs. Instant
outline.content: Introduce the difference between 'average speed' over a journey and 'speed at a single moment.' Hook the audience by asking how a speedometer knows your speed if you haven't traveled a distance yet.
outline.example: A cheetah sprints 100 meters in 4 seconds. Its average speed is 25m/s. However, at exactly 2.5 seconds, was it accelerating or slowing down? We need a way to find the speed at that exact 'frozen' frame.

storyboard.title: The Cheetah’s Paradox: Average vs. Instant
lecture_lines: A cheetah sprints across the savanna.
Average speed is total distance over total time.
But how fast is it at one exact moment?
A speedometer shows speed at a single frozen instant.
This is the mystery of instantaneous rate of change.
animations: Animate a stylized cheetah icon moving across the screen from 0 to 100 on a scale.
Display a horizontal line labeled '100 meters' (#FFFFFF) and a timer finishing at '4.0s' (#FFFFFF).
Show the text 'Average Speed = 25 m/s' in #2ECC71 below the scale.
Abruptly freeze the cheetah's motion at the 2.5s mark.
Highlight the cheetah with a pulse effect in #FF0000 and label it 'Instant Speed?'.

outline.title: The Birth of the Derivative
outline.content: Define the Instantaneous Rate of Change as the slope of the 'Tangent Line.' Introduce the formal limit definition of the derivative: f'(x) = lim (h->0) [f(x+h) - f(x)] / h.
outline.example: A magnifying glass zooms into the curve until the curved line looks like a perfectly straight flat line. The slope of this straight 'micro-segment' is the derivative at that point.

storyboard.title: The Birth of the Derivative
lecture_lines: This single-point slope is the tangent line's slope.
We call this instantaneous rate the derivative.
Mathematically, it is the limit as h reaches zero.
The formula captures change at a specific moment.
This is the foundation of all calculus.
animations: Show Point B overlapping Point A, making the interval 'h' vanish.
Transform the Secant Line into a purple 'Tangent Line' (#9B59B6) touching only Point A.
Fade in the formal limit definition: f'(x) = lim(h->0) [f(x+h)-f(x)]/h in #FFFFFF.
Highlight the 'lim(h->0)' part of the formula in #F1C40F.
Pulse the Tangent Line to emphasize it represents the 'Instantaneous Rate'.

2.  **Animation Stability**:

    *   Added a safety check in the `update_secant` function to avoid division-by-zero or zero-length vectors when point B overlaps point A.
3.  **Visual Improvements**:
    *   Adjusted the grid positioning to ensure the `formula` and `axes` are clearly separated and don't overlap the lecture text or the title.
    *   Refined the scale and stroke width of the tangent line pulse for better visual emphasis.
    *   Set the `axes` color to `GREY` for better contrast with the plot and labels.
4.  **Consistency**: Ensured all lecture line highlighting follows the required pattern (previous line returns to `WHITE`, current line becomes `YELLOW`).

        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

section_1.title: The Cheetah’s Paradox: Average vs. Instant
section_1.content: Introduce the difference between 'average speed' over a journey and 'speed at a single moment.' Hook the audience by asking how a speedometer knows your speed if you haven't traveled a distance yet.
section_1.example: A cheetah sprints 100 meters in 4 seconds. Its average speed is 25m/s. However, at exactly 2.5 seconds, was it accelerating or slowing down? We need a way to find the speed at that exact 'frozen' frame.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: The Slope of a Secant Line
section_2.content: Review the concept of slope (rise over run) between two points on a curve. This represents the average rate of change. Visually represent this as a 'Secant Line' cutting through a graph.
section_2.example: On a distance-time graph (y = x²), draw a line connecting Point A (1, 1) and Point B (3, 9). Slope = (9-1)/(3-1) = 4. This is the average speed between 1 and 3 seconds.

section_3.title: The 'Zooming In' Technique (The Limit Concept)
section_3.content: Animate Point B moving closer and closer to Point A. As the interval (h) between the points shrinks toward zero, the secant line rotates and begins to look like it only touches the curve at one point.
section_3.example: Visualizing the interval shrinking: first from 2 seconds, then 1 second, then 0.1, 0.01... until the two points are nearly overlapping. The gap 'h' is vanishing.

section_4.title: The Birth of the Derivative
section_4.content: Define the Instantaneous Rate of Change as the slope of the 'Tangent Line.' Introduce the formal limit definition of the derivative: f'(x) = lim (h->0) [f(x+h) - f(x)] / h.
section_4.example: A magnifying glass zooms into the curve until the curved line looks like a perfectly straight flat line. The slope of this straight 'micro-segment' is the derivative at that point.

section_5.title: The 'Power' in Action
section_5.content: Demonstrate the power of the derivative as a function that gives the slope at any point. Show that we no longer need to calculate 'rise over run' manually if we know the derivative rule.
section_5.example: If the cheetah's position is f(t) = t², its speed at any time 't' is f'(t) = 2t. At exactly 3 seconds, the cheetah is going exactly 6 m/s. We have turned a static curve into a dynamic measurement of change.

section_6.title: Summary: The Snapshot of Change
section_6.content: Recap that the derivative is the 'instantaneous' version of a rate of change. It is the bridge between algebra (two points) and calculus (one point).
section_6.example: Visual recap: A car driving on a hilly road. The steepness of the hill at the exact spot the tires touch the ground is the derivative of the road's height.

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Let's move the second point closer to the first.",
            "The interval between them, h, starts to shrink.",
            "As h approaches zero, the secant line rotates.",
            "Zooming in, the curve begins to look straight.",
            "The two points eventually merge into one."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The 'Zooming In' Technique", lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        h_color = "#2ECC71"
        secant_color = "#E74C3C"
        point_a_color = "#3498DB"
        point_b_color = "#F1C40F"

        # Math Params
        def f(x):
            return 0.4 * (x**2)
        
        # Origin for plot (Right side)
        plot_origin = self.grid['F2'] 
        
        def math_to_screen(x, y):
            # Scale math units to screen units (roughly 1 unit = 1 grid square)
            return plot_origin + np.array([x * 1.1, y * 1.1, 0])

        # --- Setup Mobjects ---
        # 1. Curve
        curve = ParametricFunction(
            lambda t: math_to_screen(t, f(t)),
            t_range=[0, 3.5],
            color=GRAY_A
        )
        
        # 2. Points and Trackers
        x_a = 1.0
        x_b_start = 3.2
        h_tracker = ValueTracker(x_b_start)
        
        dot_a = Dot(math_to_screen(x_a, f(x_a)), color=point_a_color)
        label_a = Text("A", font_size=18, color=point_a_color).next_to(dot_a, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        dot_b = Dot(math_to_screen(h_tracker.get_value(), f(h_tracker.get_value())), color=point_b_color)
        label_b = Text("B", font_size=18, color=point_b_color)
        label_b.add_updater(lambda m: m.next_to(dot_b, UP, buff=0.1))

        # 3. h Interval line and label
        h_line = Line(color=h_color, stroke_width=4)
        h_label = MathTex("h", color=h_color, font_size=24)
        
        def update_h_line(line):
            curr_x_b = h_tracker.get_value()
            line.set_points_as_corners([
                math_to_screen(x_a, 0.1), 
                math_to_screen(curr_x_b, 0.1)
            ])
            
        def update_h_label(lbl):
            curr_x_b = h_tracker.get_value()
            lbl.move_to(math_to_screen((x_a + curr_x_b)/2, -0.2))
            if curr_x_b - x_a < 0.2:
                lbl.set_opacity(0)
            else:
                lbl.set_opacity(1)

        h_line.add_updater(update_h_line)
        h_label.add_updater(update_h_label)

        # 4. Secant Line
        secant_line = Line(color=secant_color, stroke_width=3)
        
        def update_secant(line):
            curr_x_b = h_tracker.get_value()
            p1 = math_to_screen(x_a, f(x_a))
            p2 = math_to_screen(curr_x_b, f(curr_x_b))
            direction = p2 - p1
            norm = np.linalg.norm(direction)
            if norm < 0.001:
                # Tangent approx at A (derivative of 0.4x^2 at x=1 is 0.8)
                direction = np.array([1.0, 0.8, 0.0])
                norm = np.linalg.norm(direction)
                direction = direction / norm
            else:
                direction = direction / norm
            
            line.set_points_as_corners([
                p1 - direction * 1.5,
                p1 + direction * 2.5
            ])
            
        secant_line.add_updater(update_secant)
        
        # Initial Add
        self.add(curve, dot_a, label_a, dot_b, label_b, secant_line)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "Let's move the second point closer to the first."
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(point_b_color))
        dot_b.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(math_to_screen(h_tracker.get_value(), f(h_tracker.get_value()))))
        self.play(h_tracker.animate.set_value(2.5), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "The interval between them, h, starts to shrink."
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(h_color))
        self.add(h_line, h_label)
        self.play(h_tracker.animate.set_value(2.0), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "As h approaches zero, the secant line rotates."
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(secant_color))
        self.play(h_tracker.animate.set_value(1.5), run_time=3)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # "Zooming in, the curve begins to look straight."
        # Clear updaters for stable scaling
        h_line.clear_updaters()
        h_label.clear_updaters()
        secant_line.clear_updaters()
        dot_b.clear_updaters()
        label_b.clear_updaters()

        zoom_group = VGroup(curve, dot_a, dot_b, secant_line, h_line, h_label, label_a, label_b)
        self.play(
            zoom_group.animate.scale(2.5, about_point=dot_a.get_center()),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # "The two points eventually merge into one."
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(point_a_color))
        
        # Tangent line direction calculation (zoomed space)
        # Original slope 0.8. Direction vector roughly [1, 0.8, 0]
        tan_dir = np.array([1.0, 0.8, 0])
        tan_dir = tan_dir / np.linalg.norm(tan_dir)
        
        self.play(
            dot_b.animate.move_to(dot_a.get_center()),
            label_b.animate.set_opacity(0),
            secant_line.animate.set_points_as_corners([
                dot_a.get_center() - tan_dir * 3,
                dot_a.get_center() + tan_dir * 3
            ]),
            h_line.animate.set_opacity(0),
            h_label.animate.set_opacity(0),
            run_time=3
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard
        title_text = "The Birth of the Derivative"
        lecture_lines = [
            "This single-point slope is the tangent line's slope.",
            "We call this instantaneous rate the derivative.",
            "Mathematically, it is the limit as h reaches zero.",
            "The formula captures change at a specific moment.",
            "This is the foundation of all calculus."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Colors from storyboard and requirements
        TANGENT_COLOR = "#9B59B6"
        HIGHLIGHT_COLOR = "#F1C40F"
        FORMULA_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"

        # Setup Geometry (Right Side)
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-0.5, 4, 1],
            y_range=[-0.5, 4, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_tip": False, "color": GREY}
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "C2", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        func = lambda x: 0.25 * (x**2)
        curve = axes.plot(func, x_range=[0, 4], color=BLUE)
        
        x_a = 1.2
        h_tracker = ValueTracker(1.5)
        
        dot_a = Dot(axes.c2p(x_a, func(x_a)), color=RED)
        label_a = MathTex("A", font_size=20).next_to(dot_a, DL, buff=0.1)
        
        # Dot B depends on h
        dot_b = Dot(color=WHITE)
        dot_b.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(axes.c2p(x_a + h_tracker.get_value(), func(x_a + h_tracker.get_value()))))
        
        label_b = MathTex("B", font_size=20)
        label_b.add_updater(lambda m: m.next_to(dot_b, UR, buff=0.1))
        
        # Secant line extended
        secant_line = Line(color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        def update_secant(m):
            p1 = dot_a.get_center()
            p2 = dot_b.get_center()
            vec = p2 - p1
            dist = np.linalg.norm(vec)
            if dist < 0.005:
                m.set_stroke(opacity=0)
                return
            m.set_stroke(opacity=1)
            unit_vec = vec / dist
            # Extend the line visually
            m.put_start_and_end_on(p1 - 1.5 * unit_vec, p1 + 3.5 * unit_vec)
        
        secant_line.add_updater(update_secant)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show Point B overlapping Point A, making the interval 'h' vanish.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.add(axes, curve, dot_a, label_a, dot_b, label_b, secant_line)
        self.play(h_tracker.animate.set_value(0.001), run_time=3)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Transform the Secant Line into a purple 'Tangent Line' (#9B59B6) touching only Point A.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Calculate slope for final tangent line: f'(x) = 0.5x at x=1.2 is 0.6
        slope_val = 0.5 * x_a
        tangent_line = Line(
            axes.c2p(x_a - 1.5, func(x_a) - 1.5 * slope_val),
            axes.c2p(x_a + 3.0, func(x_a) + 3.0 * slope_val),
            color=TANGENT_COLOR,
            stroke_width=4
        )
        
        # Stop updaters before transform to avoid glitches or errors
        secant_line.clear_updaters()
        dot_b.clear_updaters()
        label_b.clear_updaters()
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(dot_b),
            FadeOut(label_b),
            ReplacementTransform(secant_line, tangent_line),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Fade in the formal limit definition: f'(x) = lim(h->0) [f(x+h)-f(x)]/h in #FFFFFF.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Use raw strings and explicit prime notation to avoid LaTeX compilation issues
        formula_parts = MathTex(
            r"f^{\prime}(x) =", 
            r"\lim_{h \to 0}", 
            r"\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}",
            color=FORMULA_COLOR,
            font_size=32
        )
        self.place_in_area(formula_parts, "A2", "B5", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(formula_parts))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===

class TeachingScene(Scene):

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary: The Snapshot of Change", [
            "- The derivative is a snapshot of change.",
            "- It bridges the gap between two points and one.",
            "- Now you know the secret behind the speedometer."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Draw a winding hilly road curve in #95A5A6.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Road function: y = f(x)
        # x range: grid center is ~3.0, range ~[0.5, 5.5]
        # y range: grid center is ~-0.3, range ~[-2.8, 2.2]
        def road_func(t):
            # t goes from -1 to 1
            x = 3.0 + 2.5 * t
            y = -0.3 + 1.2 * np.sin(3 * t) + 0.5 * np.cos(5 * t)
            return np.array([x, y, 0])

        road = ParametricFunction(road_func, t_range=[-1, 1], color="#95A5A6")
        self.play(Create(road), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Draw three distinct Tangent Lines (#F1C40F) at different points of the road.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Slope m = (dy/dt) / (dx/dt)
        # dy/dt = 1.2 * 3 * cos(3t) - 0.5 * 5 * sin(5t)
        # dx/dt = 2.5
        def get_tangent_line(t_val, length=1.2):
            point = road_func(t_val)
            slope_dy_dt = 3.6 * np.cos(3 * t_val) - 2.5 * np.sin(5 * t_val)
            slope_dx_dt = 2.5
            m = slope_dy_dt / slope_dx_dt
            
            # Direction vector
            direction = np.array([1, m, 0])
            direction = direction / np.linalg.norm(direction)
            
            start = point - direction * (length / 2)
            end = point + direction * (length / 2)
            return Line(start, end, color="#F1C40F", stroke_width=4)

        # Pick some points t for tangents
        tangents = VGroup(
            get_tangent_line(-0.8),
            get_tangent_line(0.0),
            get_tangent_line(0.7)
        )
        
        for tg in tangents:
            self.play(Create(tg), run_time=0.8)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Display the concluding text 'Derivative: The Snapshot of Change' in #FFFFFF at the center.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        concluding_text = Text("Derivative:\nThe Snapshot of Change", color="#FFFFFF", font_size=32)
        # Place in the center area of the right side grid
        self.place_in_area(concluding_text, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        # Add a subtle background to the text to ensure readability over the road
        bg_rect = BackgroundRectangle(concluding_text, color=BLACK, fill_opacity=0.7, buff=0.3)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(bg_rect), Write(concluding_text))
        self.wait(3)
        
        # Final Highlight
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(2)

        HIGHLIGHT_COLOR = "#F1C40F"

        # Setup Geometry (Right Side)
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-0.5, 4, 1],
            y_range=[-0.5, 4, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_tip": False, "color": GREY}
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "C2", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        func = lambda x: 0.25 * (x**2)
        curve = axes.plot(func, x_range=[0, 4], color=BLUE)
        
        x_a = 1.2
        h_tracker = ValueTracker(1.5)
        
        dot_a = Dot(axes.c2p(x_a, func(x_a)), color=RED)
        label_a = MathTex("A", font_size=20).next_to(dot_a, DL, buff=0.1)
        
        # Dot B depends on h
        dot_b = Dot(color=WHITE)
        dot_b.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(axes.c2p(x_a + h_tracker.get_value(), func(x_a + h_tracker.get_value()))))
        
        label_b = MathTex("B", font_size=20)
        label_b.add_updater(lambda m: m.next_to(dot_b, UR, buff=0.1))
        
        # Secant line extended
        secant_line = Line(color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        def update_secant(m):
            p1 = dot_a.get_center()
            p2 = dot_b.get_center()
            vec = p2 - p1
            dist = np.linalg.norm(vec)
            if dist < 0.005:
                m.set_stroke(opacity=0)
                return
            m.set_stroke(opacity=1)
            unit_vec = vec / dist
            # Extend the line visually
            m.put_start_and_end_on(p1 - 1.5 * unit_vec, p1 + 3.5 * unit_vec)
        
        secant_line.add_updater(update_secant)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show Point B overlapping Point A, making the interval 'h' vanish.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.add(axes, curve, dot_a, label_a, dot_b, label_b, secant_line)
        self.play(h_tracker.animate.set_value(0.001), run_time=3)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Transform the Secant Line into a purple 'Tangent Line' (#9B59B6) touching only Point A.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Calculate slope for final tangent line: f'(x) = 0.5x at x=1.2 is 0.6
        slope_val = 0.5 * x_a
        tangent_line = Line(
            axes.c2p(x_a - 1.5, func(x_a) - 1.5 * slope_val),
            axes.c2p(x_a + 3.0, func(x_a) + 3.0 * slope_val),
            color=TANGENT_COLOR,
            stroke_width=4
        )
        
        # Stop updaters before transform to avoid glitches or errors
        secant_line.clear_updaters()
        dot_b.clear_updaters()
        label_b.clear_updaters()
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(dot_b),
            FadeOut(label_b),
            ReplacementTransform(secant_line, tangent_line),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Fade in the formal limit definition: f'(x) = lim(h->0) [f(x+h)-f(x)]/h in #FFFFFF.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Use raw strings and explicit prime notation to avoid LaTeX compilation issues
        formula_parts = MathTex(
            r"f^{\prime}(x) =", 
            r"\lim_{h \to 0}", 
            r"\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}",
            color=FORMULA_COLOR,
            font_size=32
        )
        self.place_in_area(formula_parts, "A2", "B5", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(formula_parts))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Highlight the 'lim(h->0)' part of the formula in #F1C40F.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        self.play(formula_parts[1].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Pulse the Tangent Line to emphasize it represents the 'Instantaneous Rate'.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        self.play(
            tangent_line.animate.scale(1.2).set_stroke(width=6),
            rate_func=there_and_back,
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(2)

outline.example: On a distance-time graph (y = x²), draw a line connecting Point A (1, 1) and Point B (3, 9). Slope = (9-1)/(3-1) = 4. This is the average speed between 1 and 3 seconds.

from manim import *

    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

outline.title: The Cheetah’s Paradox: Average vs. Instant
outline.content: Introduce the difference between 'average speed' over a journey and 'speed at a single moment.' Hook the audience by asking how a speedometer knows your speed if you haven't traveled a distance yet.
outline.example: A cheetah sprints 100 meters in 4 seconds. Its average speed is 25m/s. However, at exactly 2.5 seconds, was it accelerating or slowing down? We need a way to find the speed at that exact 'frozen' frame.

storyboard.title: The Cheetah’s Paradox: Average vs. Instant
lecture_lines: A cheetah sprints across the savanna.
Average speed is total distance over total time.
But how fast is it at one exact moment?
A speedometer shows speed at a single frozen instant.
This is the mystery of instantaneous rate of change.
animations: Animate a stylized cheetah icon moving across the screen from 0 to 100 on a scale.
Display a horizontal line labeled '100 meters' (#FFFFFF) and a timer finishing at '4.0s' (#FFFFFF).
Show the text 'Average Speed = 25 m/s' in #2ECC71 below the scale.
Abruptly freeze the cheetah's motion at the 2.5s mark.
Highlight the cheetah with a pulse effect in #FF0000 and label it 'Instant Speed?'.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Let's move the second point closer to the first.",
            "The interval between them, h, starts to shrink.",
            "As h approaches zero, the secant line rotates.",
            "Zooming in, the curve begins to look straight.",
            "The two points eventually merge into one."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The 'Zooming In' Technique", lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        h_color = "#2ECC71"
        secant_color = "#E74C3C"
        point_a_color = "#3498DB"
        point_b_color = "#F1C40F"

        # Math Params
        def f(x):
            return 0.4 * (x**2)
        
        # Origin for plot (Right side)
        plot_origin = self.grid['F2'] 
        
        def math_to_screen(x, y):
            # Scale math units to screen units (roughly 1 unit = 1 grid square)
            return plot_origin + np.array([x * 1.1, y * 1.1, 0])

        # --- Setup Mobjects ---
        # 1. Curve
        curve = ParametricFunction(
            lambda t: math_to_screen(t, f(t)),
            t_range=[0, 3.5],
            color=GRAY_A
        )
        
        # 2. Points and Trackers
        x_a = 1.0
        x_b_start = 3.2
        h_tracker = ValueTracker(x_b_start)
        
        dot_a = Dot(math_to_screen(x_a, f(x_a)), color=point_a_color)
        label_a = Text("A", font_size=18, color=point_a_color).next_to(dot_a, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        dot_b = Dot(math_to_screen(h_tracker.get_value(), f(h_tracker.get_value())), color=point_b_color)
        label_b = Text("B", font_size=18, color=point_b_color)
        label_b.add_updater(lambda m: m.next_to(dot_b, UP, buff=0.1))

        # 3. h Interval line and label
        h_line = Line(color=h_color, stroke_width=4)
        h_label = MathTex("h", color=h_color, font_size=24)
        
        def update_h_line(line):
            curr_x_b = h_tracker.get_value()
            line.set_points_as_corners([
                math_to_screen(x_a, 0.1), 
                math_to_screen(curr_x_b, 0.1)
            ])
            
        def update_h_label(lbl):
            curr_x_b = h_tracker.get_value()
            lbl.move_to(math_to_screen((x_a + curr_x_b)/2, -0.2))
            if curr_x_b - x_a < 0.2:
                lbl.set_opacity(0)
            else:
                lbl.set_opacity(1)

        h_line.add_updater(update_h_line)
        h_label.add_updater(update_h_label)

        # 4. Secant Line
        secant_line = Line(color=secant_color, stroke_width=3)
        
        def update_secant(line):
            curr_x_b = h_tracker.get_value()
            p1 = math_to_screen(x_a, f(x_a))
            p2 = math_to_screen(curr_x_b, f(curr_x_b))
            direction = p2 - p1
            norm = np.linalg.norm(direction)
            if norm < 0.001:
                # Tangent approx at A (derivative of 0.4x^2 at x=1 is 0.8)
                direction = np.array([1.0, 0.8, 0.0])
                norm = np.linalg.norm(direction)
                direction = direction / norm
            else:
                direction = direction / norm
            
            line.set_points_as_corners([
                p1 - direction * 1.5,
                p1 + direction * 2.5
            ])
            
        secant_line.add_updater(update_secant)
        
        # Initial Add
        self.add(curve, dot_a, label_a, dot_b, label_b, secant_line)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "Let's move the second point closer to the first."
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(point_b_color))
        dot_b.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(math_to_screen(h_tracker.get_value(), f(h_tracker.get_value()))))
        self.play(h_tracker.animate.set_value(2.5), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "The interval between them, h, starts to shrink."
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(h_color))
        self.add(h_line, h_label)
        self.play(h_tracker.animate.set_value(2.0), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "As h approaches zero, the secant line rotates."
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(secant_color))
        self.play(h_tracker.animate.set_value(1.5), run_time=3)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # "Zooming in, the curve begins to look straight."
        # Clear updaters for stable scaling
        h_line.clear_updaters()
        h_label.clear_updaters()
        secant_line.clear_updaters()
        dot_b.clear_updaters()
        label_b.clear_updaters()

        zoom_group = VGroup(curve, dot_a, dot_b, secant_line, h_line, h_label, label_a, label_b)
        self.play(
            zoom_group.animate.scale(2.5, about_point=dot_a.get_center()),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # "The two points eventually merge into one."
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(point_a_color))
        
        # Tangent line direction calculation (zoomed space)
        # Original slope 0.8. Direction vector roughly [1, 0.8, 0]
        tan_dir = np.array([1.0, 0.8, 0])
        tan_dir = tan_dir / np.linalg.norm(tan_dir)
        
        self.play(
            dot_b.animate.move_to(dot_a.get_center()),
            label_b.animate.set_opacity(0),
            secant_line.animate.set_points_as_corners([
                dot_a.get_center() - tan_dir * 3,
                dot_a.get_center() + tan_dir * 3
            ]),
            h_line.animate.set_opacity(0),
            h_label.animate.set_opacity(0),
            run_time=3
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary: The Snapshot of Change", [
            "- The derivative is a snapshot of change.",
            "- It bridges the gap between two points and one.",
            "- Now you know the secret behind the speedometer."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Draw a winding hilly road curve in #95A5A6.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Road function: y = f(x)
        # x range: grid center is ~3.0, range ~[0.5, 5.5]
        # y range: grid center is ~-0.3, range ~[-2.8, 2.2]
        def road_func(t):
            # t goes from -1 to 1
            x = 3.0 + 2.5 * t
            y = -0.3 + 1.2 * np.sin(3 * t) + 0.5 * np.cos(5 * t)
            return np.array([x, y, 0])

        road = ParametricFunction(road_func, t_range=[-1, 1], color="#95A5A6")
        self.play(Create(road), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Draw three distinct Tangent Lines (#F1C40F) at different points of the road.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Slope m = (dy/dt) / (dx/dt)
        # dy/dt = 1.2 * 3 * cos(3t) - 0.5 * 5 * sin(5t)
        # dx/dt = 2.5
        def get_tangent_line(t_val, length=1.2):
            point = road_func(t_val)
            slope_dy_dt = 3.6 * np.cos(3 * t_val) - 2.5 * np.sin(5 * t_val)
            slope_dx_dt = 2.5
            m = slope_dy_dt / slope_dx_dt
            
            # Direction vector
            direction = np.array([1, m, 0])
            direction = direction / np.linalg.norm(direction)
            
            start = point - direction * (length / 2)
            end = point + direction * (length / 2)
            return Line(start, end, color="#F1C40F", stroke_width=4)

        # Pick some points t for tangents
        tangents = VGroup(
            get_tangent_line(-0.8),
            get_tangent_line(0.0),
            get_tangent_line(0.7)
        )
        
        for tg in tangents:
            self.play(Create(tg), run_time=0.8)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Display the concluding text 'Derivative: The Snapshot of Change' in #FFFFFF at the center.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Place in the center area of the right side grid

        # Add a subtle background to the text to ensure readability over the road
        bg_rect = BackgroundRectangle(concluding_text, color=BLACK, fill_opacity=0.7, buff=0.3)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(bg_rect), Write(concluding_text))
        self.wait(3)
        
        # Final Highlight
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(2)

            direction = p2 - p1
            if np.linalg.norm(direction) > 0.001:
                direction = direction / np.linalg.norm(direction)
                line.set_points_as_corners([p1 - direction * 4, p1 + direction * 4])
